summary: A CrashLog autoload writes user://logs/crash-<day>-<segment>-<n>.json carrying the reason, the last expedition snapshot the campaign session handed it, the content bundle hash and the engine version, and a suite proves the round-trip plus that game/scripts/ contains no HTTP client of any kind.

coordination.notes: Branched from origin/backend/b0-expedition-state at 2f51e77. Parallel lanes: the [autoload] block in game/project.godot takes one appended line at the end and nothing else, and campaign_session.gd takes exactly one line inside the existing snapshot() wrapper (B8 is adding save functions to the same file elsewhere). No Rust is touched and docs/SHIP_PLAN.md is not edited. Shipped: the bridge's expedition snapshot projects campaign_day and time_segment and no hour_of_day (godot_bridge.rs expedition_state_dictionary), so the in-world clock GDScript actually has is day plus segment and the file name is crash-<day>-<segment>-<n>.json; exposing strategic_clock.hour_of_day would have meant editing Rust, which this lane does not own, so the card's <hour> slot is filled by the segment rather than invented. The bundle hash is read through ContentCatalog (content_hash from the bundle's contentHash field), not by a second parser of game/generated/content_bundle.json. No .uid files are committed for the two new scripts: Godot's editor import pass in the gate generates them, and hand-authoring a resource UID would be inventing an identifier.

The notification hooks: crash_log.notification(Node.NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST) with nothing in flight writes no file; with pending_failure_reason set it writes crash-7-dusk-2.json and clears the flag: passed

Done-when 3, the no-telemetry scan: the suite reads all 31 .gd files under res://scripts/ with FileAccess and fails if any contains HTTPRequest or HTTPClient. The whole gate exits non-zero on any ERROR line, and check() reports through push_error, so the green Godot job is the assertion's verdict: passed

The suite needs no live bridge (no NativeExpeditionPort call, no MockSimulationPort) and prints none of verify.yml's five fallback markers; the 'Prove the real bridge loaded' step passed with it in the run: passed
Cleanup: purge_test_logs() removes crash-7-dusk-*.json before the assertions (so a leftover file cannot shift the counter) and again at the end, leaving user://logs as found: passed

Bite, executed on the scan logic rather than in Godot: a scratch game/scripts/diagnostics/scratch_bite.gd whose only mention of the needle was a comment made the identical scan (same root, same two needles, same .gd recursion) report 'HIT game/scripts/diagnostics/scratch_bite.gd HTTPClient' and exit 1 across 32 scripts; removed, it scanned 31 and exited 0. The scratch file was never committed: passed

Bite, NOT executed inside Godot: there is no Godot binary in this container, so the GDScript form of that failure was not run, and committing the needle to make CI red would have shipped the thing the card forbids: not_run

The card's crash-<day>-<hour> hour: the bridge's snapshot carries campaign_day and time_segment and no hour_of_day, so the segment fills that slot. Naming a real hour would need a new field in godot_bridge.rs, which this lane does not own: not_run

NOTIFICATION_CRASH itself is not exercised: Godot delivers it only on a real crash and nothing in the suite can provoke one. It shares one line with the close-request path, which is exercised: not_run
